content_sections.heading: KGMU Manager cum Data Analyst Job Description
content_sections.text: The Data Analyst will be responsible for managing, processing, analysing and interpreting survey data. The role includes ensuring data quality and accuracy, and contributing to analytical reports, presentations and other research outputs. Contribute to developing and refining survey tools, manuals and other research-related documents. Train and support field and research staff on data collection, data management and quality assurance procedures. Manage and maintain survey datasets and the data collection system. Monitor data collection across study sites, and conduct data cleaning, validation, recoding and labelling. Prepare analysis-ready datasets, codebooks and data dictionaries, and develop statistical analysis plans. Perform statistical analyses using STATA or other relevant software, and prepare analytical summaries, tables and reports. Ensure data security, confidentiality, regulatory compliance and documentation, and adhere to Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion, and Safeguarding and PSHEA initiatives. Plan, budget, coordinate and manage household- and facility-based surveys, studies, trials and pilot projects from inception to completion. Lead field logistics, communication, coordination and documentation processes. Act as the lead liaison with the Chief Medical Officer, CMS, MoICs and HoDs of survey facilities/districts. Oversee the development, translation, adaptation, pilot testing and finalization of survey tools and manuals. Lead training for research staff, field teams and facility personnel, and supervise research coordinators and research officers. Monitor study progress, data quality, deliverables, timelines and budgets, and prepare progress reports. Organise regular review meetings, and support reports, presentations, policy briefs and dissemination of findings. Participant identification and recruitment: identify eligible participants attending OPDs, screen them against study criteria, explain the study, and enrol them. Obtain written informed consent as per the approved study protocol. Provide family-planning counselling without bias, address myths, and support informed and voluntary choice. Data collection: collect baseline information, administer questionnaires, and complete case record forms. Data entry and records: enter data into the electronic data-capture system and maintain study records. Participant follow-up: maintain the follow-up schedule, and record method continuation, side effects and adverse events. Administrative work: prepare monthly recruitment and follow-up reports, and assist the Principal Investigator with progress reports.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in KGMU Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 4 posts: 1 Manager cum Data Analyst, 1 Project Manager and 2 Research Co-ordinators.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Applications must be sent to the HOD office, Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology, KGMU, Lucknow till 2:00 PM on 20 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for the KGMU Manager cum Data Analyst post?
faq.answer: The post requires a Postgraduate degree in Statistics, Biostatistics, Public Health, Population Sciences, Economics, Social Sciences or a related discipline. Candidates also need a minimum of 3-5 years of Monitoring & Evaluation experience.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for Research Co-ordinator?
faq.answer: The upper age limit for Research Co-ordinator is 40 years as on the date of interview.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary for these KGMU posts?
faq.answer: The pay is Rs. 65000/ month for Manager cum Data Analyst, Rs. 80,000/ month for Project Manager and Rs. 38000/ month for Research Co-ordinator. It is a consolidated sum without any other benefits.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply?
faq.answer: Send the filled application in the prescribed format to the HOD office, Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology, KGMU, Lucknow. Enclose your Biodata, experience certificate, testimonials and 1 set of self attested photocopies of all relevant documents.

faq.question: Q7. When is the interview?
faq.answer: The interview is on 25 November 2026, with reporting starting at 10:00 am. No TA/DA will be paid for attending.

faq.question: Q8. Can GNM/ANM holders apply for Research Co-ordinator?
faq.answer: Yes, they may be considered. Candidates with GNM/ANM qualification and relevant experience in family planning, reproductive health or hospital-based research may also be considered for Research Co-ordinator.

faq.question: Q9. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. The posts are purely temporary and co-terminus with the project. They are initially for 1 year, renewable for 1 year based on satisfactory performance.

faq.question: Q10. Do government employees need an NOC?
faq.answer: Yes. Persons working in government and Public sector undertakings must produce a "No Objection Certificate" at the time of interview.
